memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: Independent with ADLs, uses a walking stick for outdoor walks, reports mild knee pain on stairs.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 4/5 (recall 3 items, clock draw normal).
falls: No falls in last 12 months, gait steady, timed up-and-go 10 seconds (normal).
medicines: 6 regular (salbutamol MDI SOS, budesonide-formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD, montelukast 10 mg HS, tiotropium inhaler OD, paracetamol 650 mg SOS, calcium‑vit D3 OD). Polypharmacy – request review against Beers criteria.
mood: Reports occasional low mood, denies anhedonia.
carers: Anita, daughter.
goal: "I want to stay active enough to tend my garden and visit my grandchildren."

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Allergy to penicillin – develops widespread rash and itching within 30 minutes of taking amoxicillin for a sore throat.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
salbutamol metered-dose inhaler 2 puffs SOS
budesonide-formoterol 200/6 microgram inhaler 2 puffs BD
montelukast 10 mg tablet HS
tiotropium inhaler 18 mcg OD
paracetamol 650 mg tablet SOS (max 3 g/day)
calcium 500 mg + vitamin D3 400 IU tablet OD

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Spirometry: FEV1 1.45 L (55% predicted), FVC 2.30 L (78% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.63 (below lower limit). Post‑bronchodilator FEV1 1.55 L (59%).
Vitamin D 25‑OH: 22 ng/mL (insufficient, reference 30‑100).

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Weight‑bearing X‑ray both knees: Mild joint space narrowing medially, osteophyte formation, no significant subchondral sclerosis. Consistent with grade I osteoarthritis.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
budesonide-formoterol 200/6 microgram inhaler increased to 2 puffs BID (was BD)
All other medications unchanged.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: "Over the past week I’ve felt more short of breath after walking to the market, and I needed my salbutamol inhaler three times today. My knees also feel more stiff in the morning."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: ADLs independent, reports increased dyspnea on exertion, uses walking stick less often due to fatigue.
cognition: Mini-Cog not repeated (annual screen due).
falls: One fall in last 12 months (tripped on rug, no injury), gait slightly unsteady, timed up-and-go 13 seconds (raised fall risk) – advise strength training and supportive footwear.
medicines: 6 regular (same as before). Polypharmacy – medication review pending.
mood: Reports frustration with breathlessness, denies depression.
carers: Anita, daughter.
goal: "I want to walk to the temple without stopping for breath."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
tiotropium inhaler increased to 2 puffs OD (was 1 puff)
Add fluticasone propionate 250 mcg inhaler BD (new inhaled corticosteroid for COPD)
All other medications unchanged.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Spirometry: FEV1 1.55 L (60% predicted), FVC 2.35 L (78% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.66 (still below LLN). Post‑bronchodilator FEV1 1.62 L (63%).
No significant change from prior.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Chest X‑ray: Hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation or pleural effusion. Consistent with COPD.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Referral to Dr S. Rao, Pulmonology, Vydehi Hospital for optimisation of COPD management and consideration of pulmonary rehabilitation.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Pulmonology review: COPD GOLD group B, recommend continuing tiotropium + inhaled corticosteroid, add annual influenza vaccine, enrol in pulmonary rehab program starting Jan 2026. Spirometry stable.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: ADLs independent, reports less dyspnea after starting pulmonary rehab, still uses salbutamol SOS.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 3/5 (recall 2, clock draw mild abnormality) – negative screen.
falls: No new falls, gait improved with rehab, timed up-and-go 11 seconds (borderline) – continue exercises.
medicines: 7 regular (added inhaled corticosteroid). Polypharmacy – review scheduled.
mood: Mood improved, enjoys rehab sessions.
carers: Anita, daughter.
goal: "I want to keep up with my grandkids during their school holidays."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
Stop montelukast 10 mg HS (patient reports vivid dreams and daytime drowsiness).
All other medications unchanged.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Vitamin D 25‑OH: 28 ng/mL (still insufficient, reference 30‑100).
Calcium normal.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2026-10-10 at 09:30 with Dr Nandini Kulkarni (D06) for geriatric review.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: ADLs independent, walks unaided for short distances, knee pain mild, uses topical diclofenac gel PRN.
cognition: Mini-Cog not due (annual screen last done Jan 2026).
falls: No falls in last 12 months, gait steady, timed up-and-go 10 seconds (normal).
medicines: 6 regular (salbutamol SOS, budesonide-formoterol BD, tiotropium OD, fluticasone BD, paracetamol SOS, calcium‑vit D3 OD). Polypharmacy – meds appropriate per Beers.
mood: Content, enjoys gardening.
carers: Anita, daughter.
goal: "I want to remain independent and pain‑free as long as possible."
